Lab 6: Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) & Tableau

CMSC471: Introduction to Information Visualization (Spring 2026)

Materials Needed:

  • Laptops with Tableau installed or access to Tableau Public
  • Dataset: Sample-Superstore.xls

In this lab, you will explore Tableau, a powerful tool for exploratory data analysis (EDA) and visualization. You will learn basic operations, how to load datasets, and how to derive meaningful insights through different chart types.

Why use Tableau?

  • Tableau enables interactive and intuitive exploration of data.
  • It provides various visualization techniques with minimal coding.
  • You can use it for Assignment 2, so this lab helps build familiarity with it.

About the dataset

This is a sample superstore dataset, a kind of a simulation where you perform extensive data analysis to deliver insights on how the company can increase its profits while minimizing the losses.

Below are the some attributes in the dataset:

  • Ship Mode: Mode of shipping used for shipment delivery
  • Segment: (Categorical) Customer segment the product was shipped to
  • Country: Country in which the shipment was delivered
  • City: City in which the shipment was delivered
  • State: State in which the shipment was delivered
  • Postal Code: Postal code where the shipment was delivered
  • Region: Country region
  • Category: The category the product belongs to
  • Sub-Category: Sub-category of the product
  • Sales: Sale made in USD

Part I: Getting started

Choose one of the following two options.

1: Tableau Public (online, free)

Pros: No installation required, accessible from any device with an internet connection. Free to use and easy to set up. Allows sharing visualizations publicly with a Tableau Public account.
Cons: Limited functionality compared to Tableau Desktop (e.g., fewer data connection options). Requires an internet connection. All visualizations are public, meaning you cannot save private work.

2: Tableau Desktop

Pros: Full-featured software with advanced analytics and richer visualization capabilities. Supports local file storage, meaning you can keep your work private. Offers more flexibility in data connections and processing.
Cons: Requires installation and may have compatibility issues on some devices. Only available for free through UMD’s Terpware for students.

Note: If you can’t load the dataset using the online version or the processing time is too long (>2 minutes), please try to switch to the desktop version.

Part II: Exploring Tableau

Follow the tutorial

Instead of reinventing the wheel, we are using Tableau’s official tutorial because it is developed by the creators of the tool and ensures that you are learning best practices with the most up-to-date features: https://help.tableau.com/current/guides/get-started-tutorial/en-us/get-started-tutorial-connect.htm.

Your first task is to replicate at least the first four steps in the tutorial. You are encouraged to go over all but also make sure you finish the checklist items below.

Your exploratory task

  • Use at least two different chart types to explore different aspects of the dataset.
  • Modify visual encodings (e.g., color, size, shape) to uncover interesting patterns.
  • Try adjusting filters, aggregations, and calculated fields to explore deeper insights.

Discussion

  • Explain your findings to a classmate.
  • Discuss what worked well and what challenges you faced.
  • Reflect on how different visualization choices affect interpretation.

Part III: Generating insights

Your task

  • Identify two new insights from the dataset. An insight is a meaningful observation you discover from the data—something that is not immediately obvious and could help someone better understand patterns, differences, or trends in the dataset.

Each insight should include:

  • A screenshot of the Tableau visualization; the screenshot should include the names of the tabs you create so that we know you finish the first four steps.
  • A short description (2-5 sentences) explaining your findings.
  • Your insights should differ from those in the tutorial (try new subsets, filters, or chart types).
  • Consider business-related interpretations, e.g., sales trends, customer segments, or regional performance.

Post your two insights (in one submission) on Canvas-ELMS under Lab 6.

Checklist ✓

Complete at least the first four steps from the Tableau tutorial.
Identify two new insights using different charts or subsets. Explore data using filters, aggregations, or calculated fields.
